provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Revision of primary two work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to read simple sentences fluently.
The pupils should be able to identify sight words.

Introduction:
Today we will revise what we learned in primary two. This will help us remember our lessons.

Content:
We will start with phonics sounds. We will say and read letter sounds together. Then we will practice sight words. Sight words are words we see often like 'the' and 'and'. We will read simple sentences about our school and home.

Class activity:
Pupils will take turns reading sentences from the board. They will also play a game where they point to sight words on flashcards.

Evaluation questions:
Can you read this sentence? What is this sight word? Name three sight words you know.

Summary:
Today we revised our primary two work and practiced reading.

topics.title: Phonics: blends bl, cr, fl
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify the blends bl, cr, fl.
The pupils should be able to read words with these blends.

Introduction:
We have learned letter sounds. Today we will learn about blends. Blends are two letters that make one sound.

Content:
The blend 'bl' makes one sound as in 'blue' and 'block'. The blend 'cr' makes one sound as in 'crayon' and 'crab'. The blend 'fl' makes one sound as in 'flower' and 'flag'. We will practice saying these sounds and reading words with them.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in pairs. One pupil will say a word with a blend and the other will point to the correct blend on the board.

Evaluation questions:
What sound does 'bl' make? Can you read this word? Which word has the 'cr' blend?

Summary:
Today we learned about the blends bl, cr, fl and practiced reading words with them.

topics.title: Comprehension: my family
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to read a passage about family.
The pupils should be able to answer questions about the passage.

Introduction:
We all have families. Today we will read about a family and answer questions about what we read.

Content:
We will read a passage about a family. The passage will tell us about the family members and what they like to do together. After reading, we will talk about the family in the story and compare them to our own families.

Class activity:
Pupils will take turns reading parts of the passage. Then we will discuss the family members and their activities.

Evaluation questions:
Who is in the family? What do they like to do? How many people are in the family?

Summary:
Today we read about a family and answered questions about the passage.

topics.title: Grammar: naming words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify naming words in sentences.
The pupils should be able to give examples of naming words.

Introduction:
In English, we have different kinds of words. Today we will learn about naming words.

Content:
Naming words are nouns. They name a person, animal, place or thing. Examples are 'boy', 'dog', 'school', 'book'. We will look at sentences and find the naming words. We will also think of more naming words around our classroom and school.

Class activity:
Pupils will look at pictures and say the naming words they see. Then they will circle the naming words in sentences on their worksheets.

Evaluation questions:
What is a naming word? Give an example of a naming word. Can you find the naming word in this sentence?

Summary:
Today we learned about naming words and how to find them in sentences.

topics.title: Grammar: action words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify action words in sentences.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate action words.

Introduction:
We learned about naming words. Today we will learn about action words.

Content:
Action words are verbs. They show what someone or something is doing. Examples are 'run', 'eat', 'read', 'write'. We will read sentences with action words. Then we will act out these words to show what they mean.

Class activity:
Pupils will take turns picking an action word from a box and acting it out for the class to guess.

Evaluation questions:
What is an action word? Can you give an example? What is the action word in this sentence?

Summary:
Today we learned about action words and how to show them with our actions.

topics.title: Vocabulary: new words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to learn new words and their meanings.
The pupils should be able to use new words in sentences.

Introduction:
Learning new words helps us speak and write better. Today we will learn some new words.

Content:
We will learn new words like 'compound', 'market', 'kerosene'. We will talk about what each word means. Then we will practice making sentences with these words. We will add these words to our word bank to remember them.

Class activity:
Pupils will write the new words in their word books and draw pictures to show what they mean.

Evaluation questions:
What does this word mean? Can you use this word in a sentence? How many new words have you learned today?

Summary:
Today we learned new words and practiced using them in sentences.

topics.title: Composition: myself
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write four sentences about themselves.
The pupils should be able to read their sentences aloud.

Introduction:
We often write about ourselves. Today we will write simple sentences about ourselves.

Content:
We will write four sentences about ourselves. The sentences can tell about our name, age, family, things we like to do, and our school. We will write in our exercise books and then read our sentences to the class.

Class activity:
Pupils will write four sentences about themselves in their exercise books. Then they will take turns reading their sentences to the class.

Evaluation questions:
What did you write about yourself? Can you read your sentences? What information did you include about yourself?

Summary:
Today we wrote sentences about ourselves and read them to the class.

topics.title: Handwriting and dictation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to copy a paragraph neatly.
The pupils should be able to write dictated words correctly.

Introduction:
Good handwriting is important. Today we will practice our handwriting and dictation.

Content:
We will copy a paragraph about our school neatly in our exercise books. We will pay attention to letter formation and spacing. Then the teacher will dictate five words for us to write down. We will listen carefully and write the words correctly.

Class activity:
Pupils will copy the paragraph from the board. Then they will write down the words the teacher dictates.

Evaluation questions:
How should we hold our pencil? What makes handwriting neat? Can you spell these dictated words?

Summary:
Today we practiced our handwriting and wrote dictated words correctly.

topics.title: Reading fluency
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to read with proper punctuation pauses.
The pupils should be able to read in pairs fluently.

Introduction:
Reading well means reading smoothly and with expression. Today we will practice reading fluently.

Content:
We will learn to pause at punctuation marks like periods, commas, and question marks. This helps us read better. Then we will practice reading in pairs. One pupil reads while the other listens and helps with difficult words.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in pairs. They will take turns reading a short passage to each other, paying attention to punctuation pauses.

Evaluation questions:
When should we pause when reading? How does reading in pairs help? Can you read this passage with proper pauses?

Summary:
Today we practiced reading with punctuation pauses and read in pairs.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall what we learned this term.
The pupils should be able to answer questions about our term work.

Introduction:
Today we will revise what we learned this term and have a fun quiz to test our knowledge.

Content:
We will go over the main topics we studied this term: phonics blends, comprehension, naming words, action words, vocabulary, composition, handwriting, and reading fluency. Then we will have a class quiz with questions about these topics.

Class activity:
The class will be divided into two teams. They will take turns answering questions about what we learned this term. The team with the most correct answers wins.

Evaluation questions:
What did we learn about blends? Can you give an example of a naming word? What are action words? How do we read with punctuation?

Summary:
Today we revised our term work and had fun with a class quiz.
